# About me

::: {#about-content}
Hi! I'm Milena, a quantitative researcher interested in how social environments shape individual outcomes and inequality. I work with population-scale administrative data and survey data, applying methods from psychometrics and measurement to multilevel modelling and social network analysis.

During my bachelor's in Psychology at **Maastricht University**, I learned to think about behaviour in context. I also found a passion for the quantitative side of research, especially the challenge of measuring things that aren't directly observable, like well-being or trust. A master's in Statistics and Data Science at **Leiden University** trained me in statistical modelling, measurement, and working with complex data. For my master's thesis at **Statistics Netherlands (CBS)**, I worked with linked administrative registers covering approximately **17 million Dutch residents**, investigating how people's embeddedness across social domains such as work, neighbourhood, and household relates to their willingness to trust others.

I grew up in Brazil and moved to Belgium when I was eighteen. I spent two years working as an au pair caring for three young children, while studying Dutch at KU Leuven. Watching those children develop in a context quite different from my own made me curious about how much our surroundings shape who we become. I am currently based in Leiden.

In my free time, you will find me taking care of my lovely tropical plants, working in the garden, and having deep discussions about the meaning of life. I love learning about new cultures, reading about different perspectives, watching art house films, and going down rabbit holes about whatever has caught my attention lately. Whenever I get the chance, I also like to scuba dive.
:::
